summary: Discusses the URI resolution services needed to resolve Uniform Resource Names, going beyond simply retrieving a resource. Examples include getting aliases or a description of the resource. It is an experimental specification.

eli5.summary: A name is not the same as a place. This describes the services that can help turn a lasting name into places where the thing can be found.

questions: what services are needed to resolve urns
what is i2l in urn resolution
what is the text uri-list media type
subtitle: A small named set of operations for asking a resolver what a URI means, beyond just fetching it.

tldr.problem: Fetching a resource is only one thing a client may want to do with a URI, and no server can be expected to support every possible function.
tldr.mechanism: The memo defines short named operations such as I2L (URI to URL), I2R (URI to resource) and I2C (URI to description), and says how each must specify its operands, output and errors. It also defines the text/uri-list media type for returning lists of URIs.
tldr.outcome: It is an Experimental specification, so a service can advertise which operations it offers instead of promising all of them.

facts.label: Operations defined
facts.value: 9 (I2L, I2Ls, I2R, I2Rs, I2C, I2Cs, I2N, I2Ns, I=I)

today: RFC 2483 is an Experimental RFC. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Name the Operations
sections.content:
Retrieving the resource a URI identifies is only one operation. A client might instead want a list of aliases for the URI or a bibliographic description of the resource. This applies to both URNs and URLs. Uniform Resource Characteristics (URCs) appear in the memo only as descriptions of resources, not as identifiers.

While working on URN proposals, the authors found that requiring every server to handle every function, or every client to process varied answers, was unrealistic and a barrier to adoption. A client needed a way to find a server that specialized in the complex, or one that specialized in the simple but fast. The design criterion was simple: identify each operation with a token so that its operands, algorithm and errors are known.
sections.eli5: Some helpers only know a few tricks. So we give each trick a short name, and a helper can say which tricks it knows.

sections.title: What Each Operation Must Specify
sections.content:
The memo gives guidelines for anyone who writes a new operation. The specification should cover its operands, algorithm, output and errors. Operands must give the operation's name, a case-insensitive mnemonic, the number of operands, and the type and format of each. The algorithm is either specified completely or treated as opaque and left to the server or application.

Output must say one of: there is none, it is undefined, what the output and its content are, or that it is an object of a given type and format. Only errors that apply across all implementations belong in the specification, so availability and syntax errors are left out. Security considerations cover the service itself, not the protocol that carries it. A registration mechanism was dismissed as premature because the list is small, and the document limits its use of MUST and SHALL to cases that could harm existing systems such as HTTP and URNs.
sections.eli5: Each trick needs a short card: its name, what you hand over, what you get back, and what can go wrong.

sections.title: The Incomplete Set of Operations
sections.content:
Section 4 lists the initial operations. Almost all take one URI operand and have an opaque algorithm. Each lists the errors Malformed URI, URI does not exist in any form, no available output, URI existed in the past but is now unknown, and Access denied.

  • I2L: URI to exactly one URL, for lightweight clients that cannot choose from a list.
  • I2Ls: URI to zero or more URLs. The client should not assume anything about their order.
  • I2R: URI to one instance of the resource.
  • I2Rs: URI to zero or more instances, returned as a MIME multipart/alternative message; a single version MAY be returned without the wrapper.
  • I2C and I2CS: URI to one URC, or to zero or more URCs. The description might be a bibliographic citation, a digital signature or a revision history, and the memo does not define the content.
  • I2N and I2Ns: URI to one URN, or to a list of URNs, for a resource that has more than one name agreed by both name assigners.
  • I=I: takes two URIs and returns TRUE or FALSE on whether the server considers them equal.

For I2N the memo urges extreme care, because equality of URNs is domain specific. Both namespaces MUST have agreed that each name can replace the other without changing the meaning.
sections.eli5: There is one question for getting a web address, one for getting the thing itself, one for getting a description, one for finding other names, and one for asking whether two names mean the same thing.

sections.title: The text/uri-list Media Type
sections.content:
Several operations return lists of URIs, so the memo includes a copy of the IANA registration for text/uri-list. Lines whose first character is a hash sign are comments. Every other line is one URI, encoded per the URL and URN specifications, and very long URIs are not broken across lines. Lines end in a CRLF pair. When one URI has been mapped to a list, the first line SHOULD be a comment giving the original URI.

The registration recommends the file extensions .uris or .uri. The memo calls the media type a suggestion for simple experimental systems, and the registration marks its usage as Limited Use. Its security notes warn that uri-lists may be falsified, may help traffic analysts, and may reveal confidential locations, so external confidentiality measures should be available.
sections.eli5: It is a plain list with one address per line. A line that starts with a hash mark is only a note.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Communications with a server may be sensitive, and some servers hold information for authorized users only. Results may be spoofed, for example to send users to pirate repositories instead of ones that pay royalties. Requests may interest traffic analysts and may also be spoofed.

Each operation also lists two threats: malicious redirection, where a bad entry in a resolver's database sends clients to the wrong URL, and denial of service, where removing a mapping stops a client from retrieving the resource. The Access denied error assumes a system that can convey an authenticated concept of access control, so it should only be returned by systems that can determine access properly.
sections.eli5: A bad helper could point you to the wrong place or hide the right one. Only helpers who really check who you are should say you are not allowed in.
